Version pinning strategy and rollback/fallback policies

transcript:
Header: 2026-04-21 10:00 AM PDT | Duration ~42m | Attendees: Ava Patel (Redwood AE), Ravi Kumar (Redwood SE), Maya Thompson (Orion Head of AI), Carlos Diaz (Orion Platform), Priya Nair (Orion Security)

[00:00] Ava: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll do a quick sync — same agenda as last week, results review, model selection, pinning and fallback plans. how's everyone doing?

[00:18] Maya: good thanks, just back from the exec sync, they wanted to make sure we nail perf numbers for checkout flows — latency under 150 ms ideally on 95th, but we understand tradeoffs.

[00:35] Ravi: yeah, we looked at your traces last night, the prefix lengths are pretty short for checkout, so that's favorable. we ran the two candidate models you asked about — redwood-v1-large and rw-instruct-3b both quantized to int8 and a 4-bit q test — results are in the spreadsheet link (shared).

[01:05] Carlos: quick q, is that the same redwood-v1-large from the catalog? i saw a redwood-v1-legacy tag in the logs, i want to make sure we pin the right one.

[01:18] Ava: good call — there are two variants, redwood-v1-large (optimize-for-latency) and redwood-v1-large-eco (lower cost, slightly higher latency). when we say pin we mean pin to the exact model id + compile profile, so rollbacks are deterministic.

[01:40] Maya: can you explain fallback vs rollback again? we had some confusion last week.

[01:50] Ravi: sure — rollback is when you shift traffic back to a previous pinned version because of regressions; fallback is a runtime policy where the serving layer routes to a cheaper/compatible variant if the primary is saturated or slow. e.g., primary redwood-v1-large, fallback rw-instruct-3b-small (cheaper) or a hosted fallback. it's automated by policy (latency threshold / queue depth).

[02:30] Priya: security note — any change in model binaries or compile profiles needs to be auditable, we need an audit trail and KMS key id for model encryption. also SOC 2 questions: do you keep model artifacts in our VPC or in Redwood-managed storage?

[02:50] Ava: for the POC we hosted the model in Redwood Dedicated but customer-managed VPC peering. artifacts are logged. we'll send the SOC2 one-pager and the KMS integration doc after the call.

[03:10] Maya: great. on the benchmarks — can you walk through the 50/95/99 latencies you observed and token costs? there was a note about KV cash in the notes, what is that?

[03:30] Ravi: ha — K-V cash, i mean KV cache, sorry — automatic prefix caching cut token generation by ~15% on the checkout flow. numbers: redwood-v1-large int8: p50 72 ms, p95 142 ms, p99 235 ms; rw-instruct-3b int8: p50 90 ms, p95 190 ms, p99 330 ms. cost per 1k tokens roughly 0.9 units vs 0.45 units. again these vary by batch and sequence length.

[04:10] Carlos: is the p95 142 ms measured from the Redwood-hosted edge or from our VPC?

[04:20] Ravi: it's measured end-to-end with your VPC peering in the Dedicated cluster (the tests were run from your dev subnet). so network is included.

[04:45] Maya: those p99 tails worry me. for checkout we care about p95, but we also want graceful degradation not timeouts. how does streaming interact with fallbacks?

[05:10] Ava: we support streaming partial responses, but for short-checkout utterances it's usually single shot. fallback policy can be configured to allow a quick switch to fallback after queue time exceeds threshold — that keeps the UX from timing out. we'll show the policy config in the doc.

[06:00] Priya: from security side, we need to ensure fallback doesn't route to a model outside our compliance boundary (eg hosted public instance). can you restrict fallback candidates to those that meet our compliance tags?

[06:20] Ravi: absolutely — routing policies support tag filters like "compliance:soc2" or "residency:us-east-1". we'll add that to the recommended policy.

[07:00] Carlos: about quantization — you mentioned 4-bit tests, any stability issues with q4 on long sequences? we saw some hallucination drift in the perf env.

[07:20] Ravi: q4 tends to be great for shorter, instruction-style prompts; for some adversarial or long-context prompts we saw small regression in factual recall. that's why our recommendation is pin primary to int8 or q4f16 profile with eval thresholds and an automated rollback if evaluation metric drops.

[08:00] Maya: can we run a canary where 5% goes to q4, 95% to int8 and then measure eval delta on your eval harness?

[08:15] Ava: yes that's our suggested approach. we can orchestrate a canary with automatic metrics-based rollback (if metric delta > threshold). we'll include the canary playbook.

[09:00] Carlos: what are the metrics you recommend? accuracy, latency, and token cost obviously, any user-facing metrics?

[09:15] Ravi: we recommend a composite: intent accuracy (from labeled prompts), safe-failure rate, p95 latency, and cost-per-1k tokens. for canary we look at accuracy delta and latency delta primarily.

[10:10] Maya: about catalog variants — we tried "llama-3-13b" in-house and saw different embeddings and slightly different tokenization. is model aliasing a thing? how do we ensure the same model id across environments?

[10:30] Ava: we provide immutable model ids with digest hashes plus a friendly alias. pinning uses the digest. across Dedicated and Private, the digest ensures the same binary. we'll share the model manifest format.

[11:05] Priya: ownership question: who holds the keys for model encryption in Dedicated? we prefer customer-managed KMS.

[11:15] Ava: Dedicated supports customer KMS/HSM; for Private you fully manage keys. we'll include the steps in the KMS doc.

[12:00] Ravi: quick perf note — your 95th is very sensitive to batch size and burst capacity. if you set autoscale burst to allow short bursts we can keep p95 under 150ms with little cost increase. otherwise latency rises.

[12:30] Carlos: can you quantify cost delta of enabling burst capacity?

[12:40] Ravi: rough: enabling short burst capacity (2x for under 60s) increased token cost by ~7% in our sims but cut p95 by ~30% on spikes. exact numbers in the spreadsheet.

[13:10] Maya: question on rollbacks — if we pin to a specific compile profile, will a rollback to previous profile require model warm-up (cold KV cache) that would spike latency?

[13:30] Ravi: yes, rolling back to an old binary will lose warmed KV caches; we recommend staged rollback: 1) shift small fraction traffic, 2) pre-warm caches with synthetic traces, 3) expand traffic once metrics look stable. we'll document the playbook.

[14:15] Ava: i also want to highlight fallback vs staged rollback: fallback keeps serving through a compatible model with warmed caches, rollback replaces the binary. fallback is cheaper for immediate availability.

[15:00] Carlos: can fallback respect cost constraints? like prefer cheaper model only if it meets an accuracy threshold?

[15:20] Ravi: yes, the routing policy can include conditions: if latency > X AND accuracy >= Y route to fallback model Z. accuracy gating uses our eval hooks.

[16:00] Maya: we asked about observability — we need token-level cost, per-model latency histograms, and example failure traces. does Redwood Console expose those?

[16:20] Ava: yes, Console has per-route/model dashboards, token-level breakdowns and traces. we'll give you a demo link and temporary viewer account.

[16:50] Priya: also need audit logs for model version changes, who initiated pin/unpin, and IP allowlist.

[17:05] Ravi: audit logs include actor, timestamp, old/new model id and compile profile. IP allowlist is supported at VPC peering and control-plane API level.

[17:45] Maya: quick note on tests — our QA wants deterministic responses for a set of golden prompts; if we pin to redwood-v1-large but runtime uses fallback sometimes that will break QA expectations. any suggestions?

[18:05] Ava: you can run QA against the pinned model digest via the offline eval harness (we provide). for production you can restrict fallback for certain routes (eg checkout) so QA-critical routes never fallback.

[18:40] Carlos: ok good. one more infra question: how are model updates surfaced - do we push compile optimizations automatically or do we require explicit acceptance?

[19:00] Ravi: compile optimizations are non-breaking for most cases but we treat model binary or manifest changes as a new version. by default we won't auto-upgrade pinned versions; upgrades require explicit rollout.

[19:30] Maya: sounds safe. can you also include recommended pinning naming convention so our ops team can easily audit?

[19:45] Ava: yes — suggested: <model-alias>__<digest>__<compile-profile>__<date>. examples in the doc.

[20:10] Maya: let's talk scheduling — we'd like a canary next week (04/28) and if that goes well push to 25% then full.

[20:25] Ava: we'll prepare the canary plan and the scripts to run. one ask — please share the golden prompt set and expected labels before Friday so we can precompute eval baselines.

[21:00] Maya: will do.

[21:10] Carlos: small nit: in the spreadsheet there is a row titled "rw-instruct-3b q4t32" — what does t32 mean? transcription again maybe — it's q4_t4 or something?

[21:25] Ravi: yeah sorry that was a bad abbrev, it's q4f16 profile, i think i typo'd. will fix in the next version.

[22:00] Priya: on compliance docs — we'll need the SOC 2 artifact, data flow diagram, and the KMS integration steps. can you package those?

[22:15] Ava: yes — will attach SOC2 summary and KMS step-by-step in the email.

[22:40] Maya: any red flags from Redwood about our current infra? we have GKE nodes with GPUs and a VPN to the Redwood Dedicated cluster.

[23:00] Ravi: not a red flag; just a couple of suggestions: 1) pre-warm the canary path to avoid cold starts, 2) set autoscale burst policy, 3) ensure the prompt set used for canary includes long-tail cases.

[24:00] Maya: ok we'll prep that.

[24:20] Ava: quick recap then next steps. recap: agree primary model candidate redwood-v1-large int8, fallback candidate rw-instruct-3b-small, canary 5% with metrics-based rollback, security items for KMS and SOC2 docs, Redwood to send benchmarks and pinned config by Friday.

[24:55] Carlos: do we have any blockers for the canary? on our side just getting the golden prompt set and security signoff.

[25:10] Maya: timeline is OK, we have an exec decision on 05/05 so pilot results should be in before then.

[25:35] Priya: one more thing — are there any known regressions in recent redwood-v1-large builds we should know about?

[25:50] Ravi: nothing major; a recent kernel tweak improved throughput; we did notice a small tokenization mismatch in one minor locale, not relevant to your en-US flows. we'll note it in the changelog.

[26:20] Ava: i'll follow up with the benchmark sheet link again and the pinned config. Ravi will include perf numbers and fallback policy example.

[26:40] Maya: thanks.

[27:00] Carlos: small async question — if we want to test fallback to a hosted (not Dedicated) variant in a different region, any network implications?

[27:20] Ravi: latency will increase due to cross-region hops, and we avoid routing to non-compliant hosted variants unless explicitly allowed. we recommend only using hosted fallback for non-sensitive routes.

[28:00] Ava: ok, let's confirm owners of action items quickly. Ava will send docs, Ravi will send perf, Maya will share prompts, Priya will consolidate KMS questions, Carlos will coordinate infra.

[28:20] Maya: confirmed.

[28:40] Priya: one last quick question — can the Console alert on model drift metrics? we want alerts if accuracy drops or hallucination rates increase.

[29:00] Ravi: yes the Console supports eval-based alerts and can trigger webhooks or Slack. we'll set up a sample alert for the canary.

[29:30] Ava: great. any other questions?

[29:40] Maya: none here. thanks everyone.

[29:50] Carlos: thanks.

[30:00] Ava: end of formal agenda, we'll keep the remaining minutes for any deep technical clarifications — Ravi do you want to drill into perf numbers a bit more?

[30:15] Ravi: sure — on the rack tests we saw per-GPU throughput of X tokens/sec for redwood-v1-large (we'll attach exact table). with KV caching the effective tail latency drops a lot for short prefixes. but note that cache eviction policy matters for bursty flows.

[31:10] Carlos: what eviction policy do you recommend? lru or ttl-based?

[31:25] Ravi: ttl + size-based eviction works well for us. tune TTL to match expected session length. we'll include recommended defaults.

[32:00] Maya: thanks, that helps.

[32:10] Priya: and on audit logs, what retention do you support? we may need 12 months for some logs.

[32:25] Ava: Console supports configurable retention; for Dedicated we can set longer retention or forward logs to your SIEM.

[33:00] Maya: ok good.

[33:10] Ravi: wrapping up technical: i'll attach the perf CSV and an example fallback policy JSON (i'll label it clearly so you can paste into your infra). note: apologies for typos in earlier sheet (q4t32 etc) — fixed version coming.

[34:00] Maya: great. any blockers?

[34:10] Ava: none from Redwood.

[34:20] Priya: none from Security once we get docs.

[34:30] Carlos: none from infra.

[34:40] Ava: ok final recap in chat and i'll email artifacts. thanks everyone, see you next week.

[35:00] Maya: thanks.

[41:50] (call ends)

References/Links mentioned: spreadsheet: https://redwood.example/benchmarks/orion-2026-04-21 , SOC2 one-pager: https://redwood.example/compliance/soc2 , KMS doc: https://redwood.example/docs/kms-integration , canary playbook (doc to be attached).

Notes: transcription contains minor typos (K-V cash -> KV cache, q4t32 typo) as spoken.
